metadata.title: Claude, Debug Zoom.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether the debug-zoom skill fixes a broken Zoom integration or hands back something else, using the skill's own stated output -- a ranked hypothesis list plus verification steps -- as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that debug-zoom diagnoses, it does not repair.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 (a silent Zoom webhook; ranked hypothesis list planted, verification-step payoff)

beats.narration_text: Someone asks if Claude can just fix their broken Zoom integration. It can't — not directly. What debug-zoom actually does is diagnose it: isolate where it broke, and hand back what to check.

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('fix' -> 'diagnose') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it acts. This one is debug-zoom — one file, SKILL.md, plain language, no hidden logic. Its job: isolate where a Zoom integration broke, then route to the right reference — auth, API, webhook, SDK, or MCP. The output isn't a fix. It's a ranked list of what to check, in order.

shot.new_visual_element: A one-file folder card (debug-zoom/SKILL.md) beside five failure-category chips (auth, API, webhook, SDK, MCP)

production_viz.label: One file, one job
production_viz.mechanic: A folder card labelled 'debug-zoom/' opens to reveal a single nested file card 'SKILL.md' (teal border). Beneath it: 'one file · plain language · no hidden logic'. To the right, five small chips fade in one by one under the label 'isolates failure across': auth, API, webhook, SDK, MCP. A closing note reads: 'the output isn't a fix -- it's a ranked list to check, in order.'

beats.narration_text: Take the anchor: your Zoom webhook goes silent — no events arrive. debug-zoom reads its own SKILL.md, then works the pipeline: read the steps, execute them in order, return the result. For a webhook, that means checking the signing secret, the timestamp tolerance, and the endpoint URL — in that order, because each one rules out the next. Linear. No branching unless a step says so.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR -- a silent Zoom webhook, a three-phase pipeline strip, then a ranked hypothesis list typing in one row at a time

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR -- ranked, one row at a time
production_viz.mechanic: Title 'PIPELINE: READ → EXECUTE → RETURN' with three phase cards flowing left to right. Below, THE ANCHOR: a card reads 'Zoom webhook -- no events arrive.' Three ranked rows type in one at a time, each numbered: '1. signing secret', '2. timestamp tolerance', '3. endpoint URL'. Closing note: 'linear -- no branching unless a step says so.' THIS EXACT ROW LAYOUT RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Work through it, and debug-zoom hands back a ranked hypothesis list: check the secret first, most likely; then tolerance; then the URL — plus how to verify each one. Stay inside auth, API, webhook, SDK, or MCP, and that ranked path holds every time. Step outside it — a billing glitch, a UI bug — and the file has nothing to say.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- the same three ranked rows, each gains a verification checkmark; then two outside-scope cards struck through

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- ranked, then verified
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 ROW LAYOUT RETURNS, identical: the same three rows (secret, tolerance, URL). Each gains a teal checkmark and a short verification line beside it as it's worked through in order. Then a divider, and two cards fade in labelled 'billing glitch' and 'UI bug', both struck through in terracotta, beneath the label 'outside auth / API / webhook / SDK / MCP -- nothing to say.'

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. My Zoom webhook has stopped delivering events. Read the debug-zoom skill and walk me through what you'll check, in what order, before you check anything. Watch whether it hands you a fix immediately, or a ranked list to verify first — the list is the actual behavior. Liam, in for Bear.
